label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker (updated 10 September) — data as of 9 September 2026
contestNote: ECDC's tracker (updated 10 September, data as of 9 September) put DRC's confirmed toll at 6,942 cases and 3,349 deaths, an increase of 99 cases and 39 deaths from the prior (9 September) report, with new cases in Ituri (47), North Kivu (46) and Haut-Uélé (4). The outbreak reached a seventh DRC province on 9-11 September after a 23-year-old man died in Gwaka, Sud-Ubangi — the first case in western DRC — following a roughly three-week, 2,000km journey through South Kivu, Rwanda, Uganda, Ituri, Tshopo and Mongala. Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 by its own Ministry of Health (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths) and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after completing the 42-day monitoring period. France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. Africa CDC officials warned 22 August that the true case count may be 2-3x higher (10,000-15,000) given official detection captures an estimated 30-40% of infections, and that transmission may have begun as early as February 2026, months before the 15 May declaration.

This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases). WHO's 100-day assessment (24 August) recorded an average of nearly 90 new confirmed cases per day over the outbreak's first three months. A WHO Geneva briefing on 8 September said the response needs 1,600 more treatment beds (target 3,000 across existing ETCs, versus ~1,400 built) and 5,000 more health workers (target 9,000 at 3 staff per bed, versus ~4,000 currently deployed).

label: Deaths (2026 Outbreak)

contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 3,349 DRC + 2 Uganda = 3,351 total as of 9 September (ECDC tracker, updated 10 September), a crude CFR of roughly 48.3%. WHO's 100-day review found roughly 60% of weekly deaths recorded in the prior six weeks occurred in communities outside treatment centers; Tedros warned 2 September that up to 80% of new cases fall outside known contact lists. label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
value: ~48.3% (DRC, crude, as of 9 Sept); ~63.7% in North Kivu province
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 9 September 2026 (updated 10 September)
contestNote: Crude national CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's overall CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to a peak near 48.6% in late August and stood at roughly 48.3% as of 9 September (6,942 cases / 3,349 deaths). Province-level variation remains stark: North Kivu (1,139 cases / 725 deaths as of 9 September) sits near 63.7%, well above the national average, which responders and outside experts attribute to weaker treatment access rather than a change in virus behavior. Africa CDC warned 22 August that if the official case count captures only 30-40% of true infections, the true CFR could be substantially lower than the crude reported figure. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR; this outbreak's crude national CFR now sits at or above the top of the historical range.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — ~2,000 Frontline Workers Vaccinated of 50,000 Target; Phase 3 Trial Still Slated for October/November
value: ~2,000 of 70,000 allocated Ervebo doses administered to frontline/health workers in Tshopo and Bas-Uélé (target 50,000); 20,000 doses reserved for the Phase 3 trial, still targeted for October or November
source: WHO / Africa CDC / ICG / Healio / medicalxpress — 12 August–10 September 2026
contestNote: 20 August: WHO and Africa CDC announced the ICG approved immediate release of 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, 50,000 for frontline and health workers. WHO said 10 September that roughly 2,000 frontline and health workers, stationed in Tshopo and Bas-Uélé provinces, have received Ervebo under the compassionate-use campaign DRC launched 27 August, still far short of the 50,000-dose target. WHO cautioned 'it is not known whether Ervebo may be protective against the Bundibugyo virus in humans,' though early lab/animal data suggest possible partial protection. WHO vaccines chief Kate O'Brien said 2 September the Phase 3 trial 'should begin by October or November,' with Ervebo likely first into the trial given its existing licensure; medicalxpress confirmed 10 September the timeline remains October/November, with the trial to be implemented in Ituri by a consortium including DRC's INRB, CEPI, the Institute of Tropical Medicine (Belgium), MSF and Africa CDC. Tedros noted two additional candidates (Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV in the UK and a Moderna mRNA candidate in Canada) remain in earlier-stage safety trials.
delta: ~2,000 doses administered under compassionate use since the 27 August campaign launch, reported 10 September
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation, 12 August trial talks, 20 August dose allocation, 27 August compassionate-use campaign launch, and the confirmed October/November trial target are successive steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway alongside limited frontline-worker protection. Since the ICG mechanism's 2021 establishment, over 56,000 Ervebo doses have been allocated for DRC outbreaks combined, plus 167,000 doses in preventive campaigns across five countries.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 7 DRC provinces (61 mapped health zones + 1 newly confirmed case in Sud-Ubangi) + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker (data as of 9 September) / AP, AFP, Bloomberg — 11 September 2026
delta: Outbreak reached a seventh DRC province (Sud-Ubangi, western DRC) on 9-11 September after a 23-year-old man died in Gwaka following a roughly 2,000km journey through South Kivu, Rwanda, Uganda, Ituri, Tshopo and Mongala; a health-zone number for Sud-Ubangi has not yet been published by ECDC
deltaNote: Ituri Province remains the epicenter with the large majority of cases and deaths (5,508 cases / 2,501 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones as of 9 September). North Kivu (1,139 cases / 725 deaths across 16 of 34 zones, including Katwa, Biena and Manguredjipa) has the highest fatality rate of any affected province. Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uélé round out the six eastern provinces mapped in the 61-health-zone count; Sud-Ubangi's single confirmed case (9 September, first in western DRC, bordering the Central African Republic and Republic of Congo) is not yet reflected in that zone count. Sud-Ubangi's acting governor Jean-René Galekwa Vundawe said 38 contacts of the patient have been quarantined. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over by its own Ministry of Health on 28 July and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after the 42-day monitoring period. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. WHO's second IHR Emergency Committee meeting (24 August) maintained PHEIC status and expanded 'high risk' guidance to nine bordering states including Burundi and the Central African Republic.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 9 September 2026 (updated 10 September)
delta: National coverage fell to 84.4% (9 September) from 88.3% (7 September), back near the 5 September level (85.7%)
deltaNote: ECDC's tracker reported active follow-up at 84.4% of identified contacts nationally as of 9 September, down from 88.3% on 7 September — a reversal after two consecutive reports of improvement. WHO's 100-day assessment noted tracing coverage had climbed dramatically from just 9% in the outbreak's first week, but the metric has fluctuated week to week since (85.7% on 5 Sept → 88.3% on 7 Sept → 84.4% on 9 Sept) as the outbreak's geographic footprint keeps expanding, most recently to a seventh province (Sud-Ubangi) via a single patient's roughly three-week, multi-province journey. A recalibrated Lancet Infectious Diseases modelling study put the probability of Ebola spillover into South Sudan at roughly 69.3%, prompting a WHO/UNMISS preparedness mission to the border town of Ezo (27-28 August); no confirmed South Sudan case has been reported as of 10 September. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following its outbreak-end declaration, confirmed by WHO on 25 August. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone, and community resistance (isolation refusals, a patient escape in Katwa, blocked ring-closure in Tshopo) is separately undermining follow-up in several provinces. A WHO Geneva briefing on 8 September flagged a shortage of 1,600 treatment beds and 5,000 health workers as a further constraint on scaling up the response.
